input.question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?
input.ground_truth: The kidneys and eyes have a higher concentration of capillaries than other organs. High sugar levels in the blood cause capillary damage, thus the two are affected more. Here is an article from [_URL_3_](_URL_0_) and one from another [Reddit post](_URL_1_) in [r/diabetes](_URL_2_). Retino = eyes, Nephro = kidney, -pathy = denoting disorder in a part of the body. & #x200B; Hope that helps. & #x200B; R

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a house, and your blood is like the water that runs through pipes. When someone has type 2 diabetes (DM type 2), the sugar in their blood is too much, like if you poured too much sugar into your tea.

Now, your kidneys are like little filters in the house that clean the water. If there is too much sugar in the water all the time, these filters get tired and can get hurt. That’s why the kidneys can have problems, and we call that nephropathy.

Your eyes have tiny blood vessels, like very small pipes. If too much sugar is in the blood for a long time, these tiny pipes in your eyes can get damaged. This can make it hard to see well, and that’s called diabetic retinopathy.

Other parts of the body can also get hurt by too much sugar, but the kidneys and the eyes have lots of tiny pipes and filters that get hurt more easily. That’s why we worry about them the most with diabetes.
